- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (especially +0.08 to +0.17) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative (especially -0.22 to -0.61) — model ignores downside risk, leading to lagged corrections.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overreacts to short-term volatility, then undercorrects in subsequent periods.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag in price response to sentiment shifts — especially when sentiment turns negative mid-period.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (0.00–0.17), model often overestimates, suggesting it overweights recent momentum.
- Avoid extrapolating recent price trends when sentiment is mixed or trending downward — model tends to “hold” upward momentum too long.
- Correct for “overshoot after spikes” by reducing forecasted peak by 5–10% if sentiment turns negative within 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 3+ days, reduce forecast by 3–5% per day until sentiment stabilizes or reverses.
